paper.core_task: Benchmarking low-level visual perception and understanding abilities of multimodal large language models

contributions.name: A benchmark for low-level perception ability of multimodal language models
contributions.author_claim_text: We build a benchmark for MLLMs on low-level perception ability. To achieve this, we construct a first-of-its-kind balanced and comprehensive LLVisionQA dataset with 2,990 images with one low-level-related question-answer pair for each image.
contributions.description: Creation of a visual question answering dataset (LLVisionQA) with 2,990 images covering three question types and four quadrants of low-level visual concerns for evaluating MLLM perception.

contributions.name: A benchmark process for evaluating low-level description ability of multimodal
contributions.author_claim_text: We define a benchmark process to evaluate the low-level description ability of MLLMs, including an LLDescription dataset of 499 images with expert-labelled long golden quality descriptions, and a GPT-assisted evaluation to rate MLLM-descriptions in terms of completeness, preciseness, and relevance
contributions.description: Definition of a benchmarking process using a dataset of 499 images with expert-written low-level descriptions and a GPT-assisted multi-dimensional evaluation scheme for MLLM output descriptions.

contributions.name: A softmax-based quality prediction strategy for multimodal language models
contributions.author_claim_text: To evaluate precise quality assessment ability, we propose a unified softmax-based quality prediction strategy for all MLLMs based on their probability outputs. contributions.description: Proposal of a method that extracts logit probabilities for specific tokens (e.g., 'good' and 'poor') and applies softmax pooling to derive a quantifiable quality score from MLLMs for image quality assessment.

novelty_claims.text: While the paper introduces a novel benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on low-level visual tasks, the lack of detailed methodology, insufficient statistical analysis, and limited validation of the proposed evaluation strategies prevent it from meeting the full acceptance criteria.
